data.title: Walmart Sales Rise Powered by E-Commerce Gains — WSJ
data.description:
By Sarah Nassauer

Walmart is moving further away from relying on store sales.

On Thursday, Walmart said its sales and profits from e-commerce, advertising and other newer businesses were growing, while its store sales continued to slide.

It is a shift in how Walmart operates after starting as a discount retailer in 1962. The bulk of the chain's sales and profits still comes from U.S. stores, but that will keep changing, the company said.

Overall, Walmart's total revenue grew 5.2% to $188.8 billion in the three months ended Oct. 31. Based on its sales performance, Walmart raised its guidance for the full year.

The company has been doubling down on e-commerce in recent years, working to speed delivery and offer a wider range of products from third-party sellers to stoke sales.

More Americans now shop online. Walmart has been among the legacy bricks-and-mortar retailers most aggressively ramping up their online operations to get ahead of the shoppers' shift and fend off Amazon.com.

Amazon surpassed Walmart as America's biggest company by revenue earlier this year.

Walmart U.S. comparable sales, those from both stores and digital channels operating at least 12 months, grew 2.9% in the three months ended Oct 30. That is slightly higher than the 2.6% growth it reported the previous quarter, its slowest growth in six years.

Walmart didn't break out store-specific or e-commerce sales results. Chief Financial Officer John David Rainey said its U.S. store comparables fell in the most recent quarter, though he said the figure is less meaningful than it has been because stores help fulfill a large chunk of e-commerce sales.

"Stores and, I would argue, our delivery networks are actually becoming digital assets," Rainey said. "If you just focus on the in-store comp, that really misses what's going on in our business."

Its most recent U.S. sales figure was helped by market-share gains in its food business and hurt by pricing regulation in its pharmacy business, without which comparable sales would have been 3.6%, said the company.

Walmart's market-share gains in food were the largest in three years, said Rainey, as the company worked to decrease prices. Thanks to lower prices, Walmart has sold a million more turkeys than last year at this point in the Thanksgiving season, he said.

Yet its strongest growth came from its e-commerce, membership and advertising businesses. Its global e-commerce sales grew by 17% and 23% in the U.S. Its U.S. advertising business was up 37%.

"Our multiyear growth in e-commerce is evidence that customers are choosing Walmart because we deliver price, speed, and convenience across a broad assortment," said Walmart Chief Executive John Furner.

For the quarter, Walmart's adjusted earnings per share grew 4.8% to $0.65, above analysts expectations for $0.64.

It now expects earnings per share to hit $2.84 to $2.89, up from a previous range of $2.80 to $2.87. It also expects net sales to grow 4.9% to 5.2%, up from a previous range of 4% to 5%.

Write to Sarah Nassauer at Sarah.Nassauer@wsj.com

19 November 2026

Home REIT plc

(“HOME” or the “Company”)

Update on Litigation

The Company noted on 6 October 2026 that Harcus Parker Limited (“Harcus Parker”) announced that they had issued High Court proceedings against the Company and certain other parties (the "Claim"). At that time, neither the claim form relating to the Claim nor any particulars of claim had been served on the Company by Harcus Parker and that remains the case.

The Company announces that it received correspondence from Harcus Parker on 18 November 2026 noting that the Claimant's assessment of the current value of the Claim is approximately £135.4 million (exclusive of interest and costs).

The Company is in correspondence with Harcus Parker, but as the Claim has not yet been served or fully particularised the Company cannot comment any further at this stage as to do so may prejudice the Company's position in the proceedings.

The Company previously announced on 18 April 2024 that it had issued a comprehensive response to a pre-action letter of claim received from Harcus Parker Limited on behalf of certain shareholders. The claim as set out in that pre-action letter of claim alleged that the Company, along with certain other parties, provided information to investors that was false, untrue or misleading.  The Company's intention at that time, and subsequently, has been vigorously to defend itself in respect of these matters and has denied the allegations made against it.

The Company has previously indicated that the ability of the Company to make distributions to shareholders continues to be constrained whilst the Company faces potential group litigation or other claims, and issuance of the Claim illustrates this risk.  The Company is considering appropriate next steps, including the potential impact of the Claim on the previously announced intention to initiate liquidation proceedings to return to capital to shareholders, with its professional advisors and any relevant announcements in this regard will be made at the appropriate time.

The person responsible for arranging the release of this announcement on behalf of the Company is Apex Group.

data.title: IEA Sees $4 Trillion In Data Center-Related Investment By 2030 — Says Rapid AI Buildout Is Straining Grids
data.description:
Key points:
  • Global data-center investment hit $565 billion in 2025, while the facilities’ electricity use jumped 17%.
  • Planned data-center capacity in Northern Virginia, Texas, Denmark and Finland far exceeds what their grids can currently support, the IEA said.
  • Supply chains are struggling to keep pace with data center demand, imposing a speed limit on how quickly the industry can grow.

The International Energy Agency (IEA) said in its World Energy Outlook 2026, published Thursday, that an additional $4 trillion in data-center-associated investment is anticipated by 2030, driven by the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.

The anticipated investment covers data-center buildings, chips and other electronics, as well as energy equipment such as batteries, transformers, electricity grids and gas turbines.

However, the agency warned that grid connection delays and shortages of advanced chip packaging, memory chips and power equipment are limiting how quickly the data center industry can expand.

Data-Center Power Demand To Double By 2030

Global data-center investment reached $565 billion in 2025, while electricity consumption by these facilities increased 17%.

Under the IEA's Stated Policies Scenario, global data-center electricity consumption doubles to 1,000 terawatt-hours by 2030, with AI-optimized facilities driving about 75% of that increase.

The report also found that the global stock of accelerated servers used for AI workloads has grown 18-fold since 2020.

The IEA tracked 93 purpose-built AI data centers whose inferred potential capacity increased tenfold over 24 months, reaching 17 gigawatts (GW) as of September 2026. Once completed, these facilities are expected to have a combined capacity of approximately 50 GW.

Bottlenecks Constrain Data Center Expansion

According to the IEA, the rapid growth of data center capacity has been pushing electricity systems to their limits.

Planned data-center capacity in Denmark, Finland, Northern Virginia and Texas far exceeds the peak electricity demand their power grids can currently support, it said, adding, “not all this prospective capacity will be built”.

The agency also noted that grids are not the only constraint on new data center capacity, as supply chains are struggling to keep pace with demand and imposing a speed limit on how fast the data center industry can grow.

“Bottlenecks particularly affect the supply of advanced chip packaging, memory chips and power equipment. They are expected to persist in the coming years, and they moderate our outlook for data center electricity consumption”, the report said.

Power And Data-Center ETFs Mixed

Power and electrification-focused ETFs have also recorded gains in 2026, with the Global X U.S. Electrification ETF (ZAP) posting a year-to-date total return of over 5%, compared with over 1% for the iShares U.S. Power Infrastructure ETF (POWR) and a 2% loss for the Defiance AI & Power Infrastructure ETF (AIPO).

Among data-center-focused ETFs, the Global X Data Center & Digital Infrastructure ETF (DTCR) has risen over 9% year-to-date, while the Roundhill Neocloud ETF (NCLD), which provides exposure to AI infrastructure companies, has fallen over 43% over the same period.

data.title: Loblaw's Soft Grocery Sales Temper a Broadly Strong 3Q — Market Talk
data.description: Loblaw's food sales were disappointing, despite a broadly strong 3Q, says TD Cowen's Brian Morrison in a report. The analyst notes 3Q EPS increased 8.8%, in line with expectations and within its 8%-10% targeted range inclusive of headwinds from the timing of the PC Financial sale. While pharmacy segment same-store sales growth was strong, he says growth was "tempered" in the grocery segment. Food same-store sales growth came in at 0.6%, below Morrison's and consensus estimates of 0.9% growth. "While a deceleration was anticipated given consumer affordability pressures/tough comp, it was a "softer" than anticipated," he says. (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)

data.title: U.S. Export Sales: Commodity Highlights - Nov 19
data.description:
Source: USDA

This summary is based on reports from exporters for the period November 6-12, 2026.

Wheat: Net sales of 344,800 metric tons (MT) for 2026/2027 were up 89 percent from the previous week, but down 24 percent from the prior 4-week average. Increases were primarily for Mexico (93,600 MT, including decreases of 5,000 MT), Japan (91,300 MT, including decreases of 400 MT), Venezuela (51,500 MT), the Philippines (43,900 MT, including decreases of 1,900 MT), and Trinidad and Tobago (17,500 MT). Exports of 380,000 MT were up 59 percent from the previous week and 70 percent from the prior 4-week average. The destinations were primarily to the Philippines (181,900 MT), Indonesia (75,300 MT), Taiwan (51,800 MT), Mexico (26,300 MT), and Japan (22,900 MT).

Corn: Net sales of 1,588,100 MT for 2026/2027 were down 45 percent from the previous week and 9 percent from the prior 4-week average. Increases primarily for Mexico (926,300 MT, including 34,000 MT switched from unknown destinations and decreases of 10,900 MT), South Korea (197,800 MT), Japan (138,100 MT, including 45,600 MT switched from unknown destinations and decreases of 1,700 MT), Panama (80,800 MT), and Colombia (79,400 MT, including 45,000 MT switched from unknown destinations and decreases of 25,400 MT), were offset by reductions for unknown destinations (129,500 MT) and Taiwan (300 MT). Total net sales of 41,900 MT for 2027/2028 were for Mexico. Exports of 942,600 MT were up 9 percent from the previous week and 17 percent from the prior 4-week average. The destinations were primarily to Mexico (370,200 MT), Colombia (154,900 MT), South Korea (62,800 MT), Japan (59,100 MT), and Saudi Arabia (52,200 MT).

Barley: No net sales for 2026/2027 were reported for the week. Exports of 1,100 MT were to Canada (800 MT) and Japan (300 MT).

Sorghum: Net sales of 62,500 MT for 2026/2027--a marketing-year high--were up noticeably from the previous week and from the prior 4-week average. Increases were reported for unknown destinations (60,000 MT) and Mexico (2,500 MT). Exports of 2,500 MT were down 53 percent from the previous week and 26 percent from the prior 4-week average. The destination was Mexico.

Rice: Net sales of 34,100 MT for 2026/2027 were down 68 percent from the previous week and 51 percent from the prior 4-week average. Increases were primarily for Colombia (20,500 MT, including decreases of 900 MT), Honduras (5,000 MT), South Korea (5,000 MT), Canada (2,300 MT), and Mexico (700 MT). Exports of 15,300 MT were down 69 percent from the previous week and 70 percent from the prior 4-week average. The destinations were primarily to Mexico (3,700 MT), the Dominican Republic (2,700 MT), Canada (2,700 MT), South Korea (2,500 MT), and Israel (1,100 MT).

Soybeans: Net sales of 1,501,000 MT for 2026/2027 were up 30 percent from the previous week, but down 25 percent from the prior 4-week average. Increases primarily for China (580,700 MT, including 55,000 MT switched from unknown destinations and decreases of 79,900 MT), Mexico (307,300 MT, including decreases of 2,100 MT), Turkey (175,400 MT, including 66,000 MT switched from China, 55,000 MT switched from unknown destinations, and decreases of 10,600 MT), Spain (137,900 MT, including 116,000 MT switched from unknown destinations and decreases of 7,000 MT), and Vietnam (131,000 MT, including decreases of 100 MT), were offset by reductions for unknown destinations (188,300 MT), Portugal (6,900 MT), Pakistan (6,000 MT), and Thailand (100 MT). Exports of 1,839,000 MT were down 2 percent from the previous week and 17 percent from the prior 4-week average. The destinations were primarily to China (691,700 MT), Mexico (192,800 MT), Spain (155,500 MT), Egypt (115,200 MT), and Turkey (110,400 MT).

data.title: Wall St set for higher open on AI optimism ahead of Anthropic's market debut
data.description:
Key points:
  • Futures up: Dow 0.6%, S&P 500 1.16%, Nasdaq 2.04%
  • Anthropic IPO pricing lifts AI-linked stocks
  • Cybersecurity firms up after Palo Alto Networks lifts FY27 forecast

By Medha Singh, Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur

Wall Street's main stock indexes were on track to open higher after Anthropic priced its IPO above the marketed range, fueling expectations for a strong market debut and lifting sentiment toward AI-linked stocks after a brutal rout.

Anthropic priced its upsized offering at $83 per share, above its $70 to $78 range, raising $81 billion in the largest listing on record and valuing the AI lab at about $1.5 trillion. It will begin trading on the Nasdaq later in the day.

The listing follows weeks of selling in chipmakers and cloud companies, as investors fretted over stretched valuations, hefty spending on AI infrastructure and the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit.

"A strong debut is the tonic that the market needs after such a volatile period ... We can't underestimate the importance of this IPO. It sort of serves as a valuation for the wider AI ecosystem," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX.

Hyperscalers Amazon and Alphabet , both investors in the AI startup, added 2.6% and 4.2%, respectively, in premarket trading.

Chipmakers also gained, with Nvidia up 1.6% after falling for five straight sessions through Wednesday, when an upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment.

Intel , Advanced Micro Devices , Micron and Marvell rose between 2.4% and 5%.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius gained 6% and 7%, respectively, while data center-related companies IREN and Applied Digital climbed about 6% each.

Still, caution lingered beneath the enthusiasm, with some investors looking beyond Anthropic's market debut to its ability to generate durable revenue growth.

"After a few quarters, as the company reports results, we will know ... because it's the only way to see the adoption of AI, and that's the key to everything," said Massimo Santicchia, head of US equities at Procyon.

At 8:19 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis (YMcv1) were up 300 points, or 0.6%, and S&P 500 E-minis were up 85.5 points, or 1.16%. Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 555.25 points, or 2.04%.

The S&P 500 fell for a fifth straight session on Wednesday, with hawkish minutes from the US Federal Reserve's latest meeting also weighing on sentiment.

Nearly all Fed officials saw a need for more rate increases if the economy performed as projected, according to the minutes from the central bank's October policy meeting, while a few warned that inflation could be stickier than anticipated and require tighter policy.

Investors will now parse remarks from several Fed officials due later on Thursday.

Traders are pricing in a near-certainty of a 25-basis-point hike at the Fed's December meeting and about an 8% chance of a 50-basis-point move, according to LSEG data.

Among other movers, Palo Alto Networks shares jumped 9.7% after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue forecast, helping drive gains of 4% to 6% in peers CrowdStrike , Cloudflare , Okta and Zscaler .

Walmart was down 1% even as the retail giant slightly raised its annual targets.

data.title: Activist Carronade raises Brookdale stake above 5%, wants changes - Reuters

Activist Carronade Capital has raised its stake in Brookdale Senior Living  above 5% and wants ‌the largest operator of senior housing in the US to increase its share price.

Carronade is looking for changes in how the company allocates its capital and how it looks at its M&A strategy, according to a Reuters report on Thursday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Carronade owned a ~4% stake in Brookdale as of Sept. 30.

data.title: Egypt turns to Poland as it explores government-brokered wheat deals
data.description:
By Sarah El Safty and Michael Hogan

Egypt agreed last month to purchase around 200,000 metric tons of Polish wheat from state-backed Elewarr and is discussing buying more, traders familiar with the government-brokered talks told Reuters.

Poland's deputy agriculture minister Małgorzata Gromadzka said last month that Elewarr had signed a contract in Egypt, while the company's CEO Marcin Roszczyk said initial deliveries would total a few hundred thousand tons and rise over time.

Egypt, one of the world's largest wheat importers, is stepping up efforts to diversify supplies and reduce its reliance on traditional procurement channels in the face of disruptions to Black Sea exports, the traders said.

Its state buyer Future of Egypt has also held discussions with officials from Russia and Ukraine on potential wheat purchases, traders said. Market participants estimated these broader talks with governments could involve up to 1 million tons over several months.

Reuters could not independently confirm these agreements or determine the commercial terms of the Polish deal, including whether it was concluded at market-based prices under standard commercial terms or involved any government support mechanisms, barter arrangements or other concessions.

Future of Egypt, Elewarr and the Polish government did not respond to requests for comment.

Egypt relies heavily on imports for a subsidised bread programme that supports tens of millions of people. Russia and Ukraine accounted for more than 82% of Egypt's wheat imports in the first half of 2026, data seen by Reuters shows.

Several traders said they doubted whether the talks would lead to large purchases, adding that even deals facilitated through diplomatic channels would ultimately be executed on commercial terms or through private suppliers.

"The Egyptians think they can get better prices if they buy in bulk, but it would be very difficult to do and would have to eventually be done via private companies or on commercial terms," one said.

RESERVES SUFFICIENT FOR SEVERAL MONTHS

The discussions do not appear to reflect immediate supply concerns. Egypt bought a record volume of wheat from local farmers this year, and authorities have repeatedly said reserves are sufficient to cover domestic demand for several months.

Traders said Egypt appears to be seeking cheaper and more secure long-term supplies amid market uncertainty.

Benchmark Chicago wheat futures have risen more than 15% since the start of July, largely due to Black Sea disruption.

Future of Egypt took over responsibility for strategic wheat imports from the General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) in 2024. Unlike GASC, which typically bought wheat through large international tenders, the state buyer has increasingly relied on direct negotiations with global grain suppliers.

It recently returned to the import market after months on the sidelines, Reuters reported last month, with supplies sourced from countries including France and Bulgaria.

data.title: Johnson & Johnson Seeks Expanded FDA Approval for Caplyta in Bipolar Mania
data.description:
By Colin Kellaher

Johnson & Johnson has filed for expanded U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for its Caplyta antipsychotic medication in bipolar mania.

J&J said the filing seeks approval of Caplyta for the treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in adults, adding that a green light would mark the fifth approved use of the drug in adults.

The New Brunswick, N.J., drugmaker last week said Caplyta had met its key goals in a second late-stage study in bipolar mania.

Caplyta, which is already approved for uses in depressive episodes associated with bipolar I or II disorder, schizophrenia and major depressive disorder, was the key assets in J&J's $14.6 billion acquisition of Intra-Cellular Therapies last year.

data.title: BYPG Forms Strategic Partnership with GCM Grosvenor to Scale High-Power Manufacturing Real Estate Strategy
data.description:
Strategic partnership will target high-powered manufacturing assets with up to $480 Million in investment capacity

AUSTIN, Texas, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Blue Yonder Property Group ("BYPG"), a thematic real estate investment firm focused on high-power manufacturing assets, today announced a strategic partnership with GCM Grosvenor (Nasdaq: GCMG), a leading middle market real estate platform builder and GP stakes investor. GCM Grosvenor has invested an initial $62.5 million to launch the platform, which is structured to scale up to $300 million of equity over time. With the initial investment, BYPG and GCM Grosvenor intend to build a portfolio of high-powered manufacturing facilities across high-growth U.S. markets representing approximately $480 million in aggregate property value. As part of the partnership, GCM Grosvenor will join BYPG's Board of Directors.

Founded in 2023 by Bobby Dillard and Tyler Buckler, BYPG is vertically integrated across acquisitions, asset management, development, and operations. Its principals previously led Cielo Property Group, where they executed more than $800 million in retail and office investments between 2010 and 2022. Their approach has been to identify sector shifts early, from post-crisis suburban retail to creative and technology office, and to execute directly as developers and operators. Since forming BYPG, the team has developed 250,000 square feet of bulk logistics space and repositioned 135,000 square feet of infill shallow-bay industrial.

The platform will target manufacturing facilities with in-place power infrastructure, serving manufacturers in aerospace and defense, electrification, energy, advanced materials and the digital infrastructure supply chain, with initial focus on Dallas–Fort Worth, Houston, Austin–San Antonio, Phoenix and the Carolinas' I-85 corridor. The strategy seeks to capitalize on the rapidly growing demand for manufacturing facilities with sufficient power, amid increasing constraints on the U.S. power grid.

Manufacturing now accounts for 20 percent of new industrial leasing in the Southeast and Central U.S., up from 13 percent before the pandemic, yet larger users face one- to two-year delays to secure sufficient power, according to PwC and the Urban Land Institute's Emerging Trends in Real Estate 2026. For those users, a building with power already in place is the fastest path to production. By acquiring and repositioning high-powered facilities, BYPG aims to capitalize on this supply-demand imbalance, turning existing grid capacity into ready-to-operate manufacturing space, and helping close the gap between where demand is growing and where power is available.

The first acquisition under the strategy, 2000 Clovis Barker Road in San Marcos, Texas, is a 75,276-square-foot, crane-served manufacturing facility on approximately 30 acres along the I-35 corridor between Austin and San Antonio. The property benefits from 2.5 megawatts of secured power capacity, and BYPG has executed a long-term lease with an established national industrial pipe fabrication company that will fully occupy the facility at closing.

Ermias Nessibu, Executive Director, Real Estate at GCM Grosvenor, said, "Our real estate strategy is built on partnering with specialized operators and helping them scale into institutional investment management platforms. Bobby, Tyler and the BYPG team have a proven track record of identifying emerging opportunities and executing in operationally complex sectors. Growing demand for high-power manufacturing facilities is colliding with limited suitable inventory, high development barriers and constrained access to power. We believe these structural supply-demand dynamics create a compelling investment opportunity, and we look forward to partnering with BYPG to build a leading institutional platform focused on this underserved segment of the industrial market "

Bobby Dillard, CEO and Co-Chief Investment Officer of BYPG, added, "We're grateful to GCM Grosvenor for their partnership and for the conviction they've shown in our team and this strategy. Power capacity has become one of the hardest things to replicate in industrial real estate, and manufacturers increasingly decide where to grow based on where it's available. GCM's partnership allows us to assemble a portfolio of these hard-to-replace assets at scale and deliver that capacity to the companies driving America's reindustrialization."

About Blue Yonder Property Group

Blue Yonder Property Group (BYPG) is an Austin-based real estate investment manager that builds thematic strategies around emerging market trends and dislocations. Its founders have executed more than $800 million of value-add and development investments together since 2010. BYPG's current focus is high-power manufacturing, a strategy at the intersection of infrastructure and industrial real estate that acquires and repositions existing manufacturing facilities with significant in-place power capacity and mission-critical infrastructure across high-growth U.S. markets. The firm combines operator-led execution, long-standing industry relationships and a dedicated off-market acquisitions platform. For more information, visit bypg.com.

About GCM Grosvenor

GCM Grosvenor (Nasdaq: GCMG) is a global alternative asset management solutions provider with approximately $97 billion in assets under management across private equity, infrastructure, real estate, credit, and absolute return strategies. Specializing in alternatives for more than 50 years, the firm serves a global institutional and individual client base through a team of approximately 550 professionals. GCM Grosvenor is headquartered in Chicago, with offices in New York, Toronto, London, Frankfurt, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Seoul, and Sydney. For more information, visit gcmgrosvenor.com.
